# Rooted Memories

Rooted Memories is a private family archive and family tree app designed to help families organise, preserve, and pass down their memories over time.

## Core Concept

Rooted Memories combines a family tree with structured memory storage. Each family member is represented as a “leaf”, and photos, stories, and memories are attached directly to the people they belong to.

This creates a clear and organised family history that grows naturally over the years.

## What It Is

Rooted Memories is a private family archive built for both everyday family life and long term memory preservation.

It is not social media and not general cloud storage. Instead of memories being lost in camera rolls, folders, or group chats, Rooted Memories keeps them organised around the people and relationships that matter most.

Families can build a living history together as children grow up, milestones happen, and generations contribute over time.

## Key Features

- Private family tree structure
- Individual profiles (“leaves”) for each family member
- Photos and stories organised by person
- Timeline-based family memory organisation
- Multi-generation contribution and collaboration
- Invite-only private family access
- Built-in successor system for long term continuity
- Designed for long term family archive use
- Built to be handed down across generations

## Why It Exists

Most family memories are scattered across phones, camera rolls, cloud storage, and messaging apps with no structure and no lasting context.

Rooted Memories exists to turn those disconnected memories into a structured family archive that grows over time.

Parents can document their children’s lives as they grow, families can preserve shared history together, and future generations can eventually look back on a meaningful record of their family story.

## Use Cases

- Create a private family archive for your children and future generations
- Build a digital family tree with real memories attached
- Preserve family photos, milestones, and stories in one place
- Organise memories by person instead of folders or camera rolls
- Allow family members to contribute to a shared family history
- Build a living archive that grows year after year
- Create something meaningful that can eventually be handed down
